# HW1: Import Data from Statistical Packages and Database Management Systems

## Part A: Importing Data from a Statistical Package

In this part, I created a small dataset containing fictional hospital doctors. The dataset includes their department, years of experience, and number of patients seen per day.

I then saved the data as an SPSS file and imported it back into R to practice importing data from a statistical package.

### Step 1: Create the hospital doctors' data

```{r}
doctors <- data.frame(
  Doctor_ID = c(101, 102, 103, 104, 105),
  Doctor_Name = c("Dr. Alice", "Dr. David", "Dr. Grace",
                  "Dr. John", "Dr. Sarah"),
  Department = c("Cardiology", "Pediatrics", "Emergency",
                 "Radiology", "Surgery"),
  Years_Experience = c(8, 5, 10, 6, 12),
  Patients_Per_Day = c(15, 20, 25, 12, 18)
)

print(doctors)
```

### Step 2: Export the data to an SPSS file

```{r}
library(haven)

write_sav(doctors, "hospital_doctors.sav")
```

### Step 3: Import the SPSS file into R

```{r}
imported_doctors <- read_sav("hospital_doctors.sav")

print(imported_doctors)
head(imported_doctors)
```
## Part B: Importing Data from a Database Management System

In this part, I will use an mySql database to store the fictional hospital doctors' data. I will then connect to the database and import the data into R.


```{r}
# Connect R to the hospital database
library(DBI)
library(RMariaDB)

con <- dbConnect(
  RMariaDB::MariaDB(),
  host = "localhost",
  port = 3306,
  user = "root",
  password = "",
  dbname = "hospital_db"
)

# Check the database connection
dbListTables(con)
# Save the doctors' dataset into MySQL

dbWriteTable(con, "doctors", doctors,
             overwrite = TRUE, row.names = FALSE)

# Check the records stored in MySQL

dbReadTable(con, "doctors")
# Close the database connection
dbDisconnect(con)
```
## Part C: Importing Data from an API

In this part, I will use a public API to retrieve sample data and import it into R. This helps me understand how data can be collected from an online source.

```{r}

# Load the package
library(jsonlite)

# Import data from the API
api_url <- "https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users"
api_data <- fromJSON(api_url)

# Because the API was disarranged this help to select the data needed
simple_data <- api_data[, c("id", "name", "username", "email")]

print(simple_data, row.names = FALSE)

```
